key_insight: Fe or Cr substitution at Ni grain-boundary planes increases cohesion, with strengthening governed by element type and local atomic structure.
engineering_relevance: Atomistically predicted cohesion parameters can inform continuum fracture models for multicomponent Ni-based alloys.
method: Compute DFT rigid-body separation curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni grain boundaries.
Extract work of separation and peak traction using the universal binding energy relation.
Benchmark ML interatomic potentials against DFT, then sample finer alloying increments and ternary compositions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative DFT agreement for one tested ML potential on both cohesion metrics and extends the analysis to Ni56Fe20Cr24.
watch_item: Binary alloying trends do not quantitatively capture Fe–Cr interplay; explicit ternary calculations remain necessary.
paper_title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
